capabilities: Run local shells in terminal tabs, splits, and windows
Create and launch reusable terminal, command, and link workflows
Send editor selections, note content, and paths into the terminal
Open file references printed in terminal output
Hand off vault and editor context to AI CLI sessions
extras: Desktop-only (native PTY backend). Downloads the matching native PTY server binary from GitHub Releases on first use; offline mode disables download and update checks. No telemetry or analytics. Also installable via BRAT for early updates.
motivation: The author built it for people who already live in Obsidian and do real work in a terminal, wanting a terminal aligned with vault and editor context.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in terminal, so users must switch to an external terminal app and lose access to their vault and editor context.

relations.evidence: Powered by xterm.js and a native Rust PTY backend
Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode integrations can inherit active note context from Obsidian.
Codex uses a vault-local Skill at .agents/skills/termy-obsidian-context/SKILL.md.
Claude Code and OpenCode use Termy's IDE bridge
the built-in dsh-TUI launcher receives Obsidian editor selections through dsh-TUI's protocol-v2 loopback bridge

summary: Terminal emulator plugin that runs local shells inside Obsidian with split panes, reusable workflows, and AI CLI context handoff.
